name: Flutter Navigator / Router
summary: Flutter's built-in navigation system. Navigator provides stack-based imperative navigation, while Router supports declarative routing, deep-link handling, and browser history integration without requiring a third-party routing package.
advantages: Built into Flutter with no additional routing package
Navigator provides straightforward stack-based push and pop navigation
Router can handle deep links and synchronize navigation with browser history
Provides full control over RouteInformationParser, RouterDelegate, Navigator pages, and route stacks
tradeoffs: Direct Router API configuration is more involved than using a higher-level routing package
Flutter does not recommend named routes for most applications because of limitations around customizable deep-link behavior and browser forward navigation
Complex multi-Navigator or URL-driven applications require more manual routing infrastructure when no routing package is used
recommendedFor: Small applications without complex deep-link requirements using Navigator
Applications that need full low-level control over routing behavior
Teams that intentionally want to avoid an additional routing dependency

verification.reason: Flutter official navigation documentation directly covers the relevant capabilities and limitations.
